title: unify-rate-window-retry-after-and-idempotency-resolution-in-openai-bridge
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: In production we observed intermittent client-visible 429/RateLimit errors during streaming sessions where backpressure and cross-region retries led to duplicated retry timers and ambiguous Retry-After semantics. Additionally, idempotency resolution in the OpenAI compatibility shim treated X-Redwood-Idempotency keys as purely local and could re-run tool calls across fallback routes, causing duplicate external side-effects. This PR unifies three related concerns into a single, minimal-surface change: (1) normalize rate-limit/time-window headers from upstreams and expose a single canonical Retry-After value to the OpenAI shim, (2) add a bounded retry-window policy for streaming connections to avoid overlapping timers, and (3) tighten idempotency resolution to include route-fingerprint and last-success timestamp to prevent cross-route replays.

Summary of changes: single continuous commit series implementing normalization and safety checks, tests, and docs. Key points: consolidate RateLimit-* and Retry-After header parsing into a shared parser; expose a best-effort canonical_retry_after_ms in the OpenAI compatibility response pipeline; enforce a streaming_retry_window_ms config (default 2000ms) that deduplicates concurrent retry attempts per-client/request hash; store idempotency records with route_fingerprint and last_success_ts and refuse replays across non-matching route_fingerprint.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests for header parsing and window dedupe
- [x] integration test: streaming session restart does not cause duplicate tool calls
- [x] e2e regression test against openai-compat shim
- [x] docs: compatibility notes and migration guidance

Commits (high level):
- normalize: shared header parser for Retry-After and RateLimit windows (parser/rate_headers.go, parser/rate_headers_test.go)
- streaming: add streaming_retry_window to runtime config and dedupe logic (runtime/stream_manager.go)
- idempotency: augment idempotency store entries with route_fingerprint & last_success_ts and enforcement (services/idempotency_store.go)
- openai-shim: surface canonical_retry_after_ms in /v1/responses header mapping and error body (adapters/openai_compat/response_mapper.go)
- tests/docs: add unit/integration tests and note in docs/compatibility/openai-rate-limits.md

Files changed (high level):
- parser/rate_headers.go (new)
- parser/rate_headers_test.go (new)
- runtime/stream_manager.go (modified)
- services/idempotency_store.go (modified)
- adapters/openai_compat/response_mapper.go (modified)
- adapters/openai_compat/streaming_adapter_test.go (new)
- docs/compatibility/openai-rate-limits.md (modified)
- config/defaults.yaml (modified)

Small illustrative snippet (response_mapper.go):
- old: "retry_after = ctx.headers.get('Retry-After') || 0"
- new: "retry_after = parser.ParseCanonicalRetryAfter(ctx.headers) // returns ms or 0 if unknown"

Testing and validation:
- added unit tests covering RFC-compliant "Retry-After" (delta-seconds, HTTP-date), nonstandard RateLimit-Window headers (RateLimit-Window, X-RateLimit-Window), and corrupt values (fallback to best-effort estimate).
- streaming integration test simulates transient region failover + backpressure to ensure only a single retry timer per request hash fires within streaming_retry_window_ms.
- idempotency tests ensure requests with same idempotency key but different route_fingerprint are not replayed; same key+fingerprint within last_success_ts returns 409/Conflict per OpenAI semantics.

Operational notes / rollout:
- defaults.yaml introduces streaming_retry_window_ms: 2000 and idempotency_grace_window_ms: 300000 (5min) which is conservative; operators can tune via config.
- backward-compatible: if upstream does not send RateLimit-* headers we fall back to Retry-After or to a safe circuit-breaker.
- telemetry: new metrics: openai_compat.canonical_retry_after_ms.histogram, stream.retry_dedup.count, idempotency.replay_block.count

Migration: existing idempotency store entries are compatible; the store will lazily backfill route_fingerprint for new entries only. No forced DB migration performed in this PR to keep upgrade simple.

Related: SUP-912 (customer reported duplicate tool runs), ENG-3019 (streaming resiliency epic).
commits: parser: add canonical Retry-After & RateLimit window parser
runtime: dedupe streaming retries using streaming_retry_window_ms
services: include route_fingerprint and last_success_ts in idempotency store
openai-compat: surface canonical_retry_after_ms and prefer it in error body
tests: add unit/integration tests for retry semantics and idempotency
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Overall this sharpens several previously ambiguous behaviors. Please add a short comment explaining why we chose 2s default for streaming_retry_window_ms and include a metric for dedupe ops.
Maya Patel (author): Added comment and new metric stream.retry_dedup.count in latest push. Also added a test that asserts only one retry timer fires in 2s window.
Leah Kim: We should be careful about clock skew when checking last_success_ts across regions. Can we use monotonic sequence numbers or include server_id in idempotency record?

Maya Patel: Good point — opted for last_success_ts + server_id fingerprint to allow cross-region rejections but still avoid identical-but-shifted clocks causing acceptance. Documented in idempotency_store.go header.
Carlos Mendoza: CI failure on golangci-lint in services/idempotency_store.go (unused import). Fixed in 3rd commit. Approving pending green CI.
Ethan Zhao: Approved. Verified integration test against chaos simulation in perf-canary lab.
merge_details: Merged by squash on 2026-02-25 by Ethan Zhao. Merge commit: squash of 5 commits. Release note appended to changelog.
release_notes: Stabilize OpenAI compatibility: canonical Retry-After parsing, streaming retry deduplication, and stricter idempotency resolution to prevent duplicate external tool calls. Defaults are conservative and tunable via config.
notes_for_support: If customers report 429s during streaming after this change, verify their upstreams' RateLimit-* headers and recommend adjusting streaming_retry_window_ms or idempotency_grace_window_ms. Use new metrics (openai_compat.canonical_retry_after_ms, stream.retry_dedup.count, idempotency.replay_block.count) for triage.
